summary: Fourteen days of high-quality CGM data show strong overall time in range but clinically important recurrent hypoglycaemia, concentrated around 23:00-03:00 and 18:00-19:00 local time. Daytime rises are often followed by delayed falls while SMB/UAM, temporary basal and Dynamic ISF are active. Because no carbohydrates or meal-strategy values were recorded or declared, the data cannot distinguish basal, meal timing, CR, absorption and automation effects reliably. The safest synthesis is to keep the current profile and automation values provisionally, prioritise structured verification of overnight and meal-linked insulin exposure, and review the permissive maximum IOB and basal safety ceilings without assigning unsupported replacement values.

analysis_steps.findings: CGM coverage and profile completeness support time-pattern analysis. Causal meal and dose-response analysis is limited because carbohydrates were not recorded and detailed treatments and loop statuses are representative subsets.
analysis_steps.evidence: There were 3,995 valid CGM entries, 98.7% coverage, an estimated five-minute cadence, no invalid or duplicate entries, and ten gaps with a largest gap of 65 minutes. The authoritative profile includes all basal, target, CR, ISF and DIA values and is declared historically applicable.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Later interpretation must use local-time glucose and account for automated insulin, temporary targets, GLP-1 notes, site events and the absence of meal-linked records.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Absent fields include meal strategies, carbohydrate entries, e-carb entries, activity context, low-treatment carbohydrates and a complete event-level insulin-delivery sequence.

analysis_steps.findings: Recurrent hypoglycaemia is the dominant safety constraint. Daytime hyperglycaemia should not be addressed by adding insulin until the subsequent delayed falls and accumulated IOB are better separated.
analysis_steps.evidence: Average glucose was 121.6 mg/dL, time in range 86.0%, time above range 8.9%, time below range 5.1%, SD 39.7 mg/dL and CV 32.6%. Local below-range exposure was 18.5% at 01:00 and 15.3% at 19:00. Recorded lows reached 41-42 mg/dL, while highs reached 293 mg/dL. Several correction windows showed falls greater than 100 mg/dL within two to six hours.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Safety interpretation depends on verification of sensor lows, preceding IOB, SMBs, temporary basal, corrections, meals and activity.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Meter confirmation, symptoms, low treatments and complete insulin history around severe lows are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: The overnight low pattern makes excess effective insulin or the 90 mg/dL overnight target plausible contributors, but late-evening IOB and automated delivery remain unresolved. Daytime highs cannot be labelled a basal deficit because undocumented meals and UAM responses remain plausible.
analysis_steps.evidence: Below-range exposure was elevated from 23:00 through 03:00, while 04:00-08:00 was comparatively stable. Glucose rose from 09:00 and peaked at 16:00 before low exposure increased at 18:00-19:00. Representative records show frequent zero and elevated temporary basal rates, so delivered insulin differed materially from scheduled basal.
analysis_steps.dependencies: A fasting-like overnight assessment requires low starting IOB and no late meal, correction, activity or temporary target. Daytime basal interpretation depends on meal-linked records and automation review.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No tagged fasting windows or complete actual target and automated-delivery history are available.

analysis_steps.findings: No CR segment can be tested without meal-linked carbohydrate and bolus data. Delayed overcorrection is plausible, but it cannot be assigned to the fixed ISF or DIA because Dynamic ISF, SMB/UAM, temporary basal and overlapping corrections alter effective insulin exposure.
analysis_steps.evidence: The profile ISF is 56 mg/dL/U, while representative variable sensitivity ranged approximately from 27.8 to 124 mg/dL/U. Correction responses ranged from continued rises to severe delayed falls. The profile DIA is 10 hours, but no isolated bolus-action series is available.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Fixed ISF and DIA should be interpreted only after Dynamic ISF, IOB accounting and meal effects are separated. CR assessment requires repeatable meals with known carbohydrate and bolus timing.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Carbohydrate amounts, meal boluses, prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage and isolated correction observations are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: SMB/UAM consistently responded to rising glucose with COB at zero. This likely compensated for unannounced or undocumented food-like rises, but substantial IOB and later lows make overcompensation possible. The evidence does not isolate an individual SMB switch, interval or dose limit as the cause.
analysis_steps.evidence: SMB and UAM were enabled, SMB was always eligible, and representative loops repeatedly showed COB 0 with UAM dosing. IOB reached 4.73 U and 5.935 U during some highs. Standard and UAM SMB limits were 15 and 20 basal minutes, with a configured interval of three minutes.
analysis_steps.dependencies: SMB interpretation depends on Dynamic ISF, DIA accuracy, meal timing, correction overlap and absorption. Dependent SMB, ISF and DIA settings should not be changed together.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: Complete cumulative SMB sequences and meal-linked COB records are absent.

analysis_steps.findings: Dynamic ISF materially strengthened effective correction during some highs and may have contributed to IOB accumulation, while appropriately weakening or suspending insulin in other circumstances. The explicit 25 U maximum IOB and 12 U/h maximum basal are permissive backstops, but the package does not support exact replacements.
analysis_steps.evidence: Dynamic sensitivity was enabled at 70%, Autosens was disabled, and variable sensitivity sometimes fell well below the fixed 56 mg/dL/U ISF. Representative IOB reached nearly 6 U. Recorded insulin totalled 275.95 U over 14 days. Derived safety caps limited representative basal suggestions below the explicit 12 U/h ceiling.
analysis_steps.dependencies: A safety-limit review should precede meal-strategy experimentation but remain separate from changes to Dynamic ISF, SMB limits, fixed ISF or DIA.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The full distribution of actual IOB, delivered basal rates and prevented doses is unavailable.

analysis_steps.findings: No numerical prebolus interval or immediate bolus percentage is supported. Daytime rises could reflect timing, CR, delayed absorption or unannounced meals, while later lows make additional immediate or corrective insulin unsafe to infer from glucose alone.
analysis_steps.evidence: The declared meal-strategy list is empty, treatment_summary reports zero carbohydrate entries, and representative treatments contain no meal-linked boluses. Therapy-response windows show both initial rises and substantial falls through six hours while automation and overlapping IOB remain uncontrolled.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Meal strategy depends on CR, fixed and Dynamic ISF, DIA, targets, SMB/UAM, IOB and hypoglycaemia risk.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: A representative recurring meal with carbohydrate amount, insulin timing, immediate bolus percentage and six-hour response is absent.

analysis_steps.findings: No e-carb amount, start offset or duration can be inferred. Delayed absorption is plausible but cannot be separated from IOB, SMB, corrections or temporary targets. E-carbs are carbohydrate absorption entries and are not equivalent to an extended bolus.
analysis_steps.evidence: There were zero carb and e-carb entries, total recorded carbohydrates were 0 g, and average e-carb duration was null. The configured absorption settings had no documented COB series against which they could be tested.
analysis_steps.dependencies: E-carb assessment requires meal-linked evidence while CR, automation and bolus strategy remain stable.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: No recurring meal has a recorded carbohydrate amount and glucose-action timeline.

analysis_steps.findings: The competing explanations are unresolved, but cumulative automated and correction insulin is at least as plausible as weak basal, CR or fixed ISF. The primary action is to keep the profile while obtaining a controlled overnight verification. Safety-limit review follows separately, then structured meal observation. No exact profile or AAPS value change is sufficiently supported.
analysis_steps.evidence: Strong CGM coverage establishes recurrent low periods, while absent meal data and representative rather than complete insulin records prevent causal assignment. Dynamic ISF, UAM dosing with COB zero, high observed IOB and delayed falls link automation to the pattern without proving a single defective setting.
analysis_steps.dependencies: Each stage should be assessed before the next, and dependent insulin-delivery settings should remain unchanged during verification.
analysis_steps.data_gaps: The most important missing evidence is a complete insulin and meal timeline through representative overnight and recurring-meal periods.

strengths: CGM coverage was 98.7% with no invalid or duplicate entries.
Overall time in range was 86.0% with average glucose of 121.6 mg/dL.
Glucose was comparatively stable from approximately 04:00 to 08:00 local time.
The authoritative profile is complete and declared applicable to the analysis period.
Representative loop records show that automation often reduced or suspended insulin when low glucose was predicted.
issues: Time below range was 5.1%, with recurrent lows around 23:00-03:00 and 18:00-19:00 and recorded values down to 41-42 mg/dL.
Daytime rises were sometimes followed by large delayed falls, consistent with cumulative correction, SMB/UAM and temporary-basal insulin but not diagnostic of one setting.
Dynamic ISF sometimes produced effective sensitivity substantially stronger than the fixed profile ISF during hyperglycaemia.
The maximum IOB of 25 U and maximum basal of 12 U/h are permissive safety ceilings relative to observed use, although lower derived caps operated in representative records.
No declared meal strategy, carbohydrate entry or e-carb entry is available, preventing reliable assessment of CR, prebolus timing, immediate bolus percentage or absorption.

recommendations.title: Keep the profile while verifying the overnight low pattern
recommendations.description: The overnight low signal is strong, but scheduled basal and target cannot be separated from late-evening IOB and automation. A fasting-like overnight review with complete insulin context should precede any profile change.

suggested_change.verification: Review several nights beginning without a late meal, correction, activity, temporary target or substantial IOB, with CGM lows independently confirmed when feasible.

recommendations.title: Review automation safety ceilings separately
recommendations.description: The 25 U maximum IOB and permissive basal ceilings offer limited backstop relative to observed use, but the package does not support safe replacement values. Review actual peak IOB and delivered-rate history before considering one ceiling change.

suggested_change.direction: Keep current values pending safety review
suggested_change.sequence: Assess maximum IOB first without simultaneously changing Dynamic ISF, SMB limits, fixed ISF or DIA.

recommendations.title: Capture one recurring meal before adjusting meal settings
recommendations.description: A meal-linked six-hour record is needed to distinguish bolus timing, CR, delayed absorption and post-rise automation.

suggested_change.observation: Record carbohydrate amount, meal and insulin timestamps, actual prebolus, immediate percentage, starting glucose and IOB, SMBs, corrections, activity, temporary targets and six-hour CGM response.

profile_recommendation.recommendation: Keep the current profile and verify the 23:00-03:00 pattern across several fasting-like nights before considering an overnight basal or target change.
profile_recommendation.rationale: Recurrent overnight lows are well supported, but late-evening IOB, SMB/UAM, temporary basal and the 23:00 target transition remain plausible causes. The stable 04:00-08:00 period also argues against a broad overnight basal reduction without a cleaner test.
profile_recommendation.next_check: Compare CGM and complete delivered-insulin history from 21:00 to 08:00 on several nights starting without a late meal, correction, activity, temporary target or substantial IOB.

parameter_decisions.rationale: Lows are frequent from 23:00-03:00, but preceding IOB and automated delivery are unresolved. Keep 0.6 U/h until fasting-like nights separate scheduled basal from evening insulin carryover.
Glucose was comparatively stable around 04:00-06:00. There is no isolated evidence that this segment is excessive or insufficient, and interpretation depends on overnight IOB.
The 06:00-08:00 period was stable with little below-range exposure. Later rises may be meal or UAM related, so a basal change is unsupported.
Daytime hyperglycaemia is present, but no meals are recorded and delayed falls occur after automated insulin. Meal, CR, Dynamic ISF and SMB dependencies prevent a basal inference.
High glucose around 16:00 is followed by increased low exposure at 18:00-19:00. Prior corrections, SMBs and temporary basal can dominate this low scheduled rate, so increasing it is unsupported.
Evening lows are evident, but their timing follows daytime hyperglycaemia and substantial automated IOB. Keep pending complete preceding insulin histories.
The 19:00 low exposure may largely reflect insulin delivered earlier. A change to the segment beginning at 19:00 is not supported without low-IOB observations.
There are no carbohydrate or meal-bolus records for this segment. Overnight hypoglycaemia increases the risk of strengthening CR without meal-linked evidence.
Morning rises could reflect meal timing, unannounced food or UAM behavior. No carbohydrate amount or immediate bolus record is available to test this CR.
Late-morning and afternoon highs are not meal-linked and are sometimes followed by delayed lows. CR, absorption, SMB/UAM and correction effects remain inseparable.
Evening low exposure argues against strengthening this CR without documented meals. The effect of preceding daytime IOB remains a major dependency.
No meal-linked evidence tests this segment, and recurrent late-night lows make an insulin-increasing change unsupported.

Some corrections were followed by large delayed falls, but Dynamic ISF produced effective sensitivities ranging widely around the fixed value. Fixed ISF should remain unchanged until automation and overlapping IOB are separated.

The overnight target may contribute to aggressive delivery during a low-prone period, but actual temporary and algorithm-derived targets varied. A precise replacement is unsupported without fasting-like target and IOB histories.
Daytime highs and delayed lows indicate that changing the target could alter both correction intensity and hypoglycaemia risk. Meal and automation dependencies remain unresolved.
Low exposure increases after 23:00, making this target a review candidate, but late-evening IOB and automated delivery have not been excluded. No supported alternative value is available.
Delayed falls make insulin-action accounting important, but no isolated bolus decay curve establishes that 10 hours is wrong. DIA should not be changed with ISF, Dynamic ISF or SMB settings.

SMB/UAM responds to genuine food-like rises with COB zero, but may contribute to accumulated IOB. Disabling it could worsen undocumented-meal highs, and the package does not isolate the enable switches from Dynamic ISF, DIA and meal effects.
The activation settings are internally consistent, and UAM is not evidence of duplicate COB counting. Complete eligibility histories are absent, so no individual switch change is supported.

parameter_decisions.current_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.suggested_value: smb_interval_minutes=3 min; max_smb_basal_minutes=15 min; max_uam_smb_basal_minutes=20 min
parameter_decisions.rationale: Recurrent lows and high IOB justify review, but complete cumulative SMB sequences are absent. Dynamic ISF, repeated corrections, DIA and delayed absorption remain competing explanations, so changing interval or dose limits is unsupported.

parameter_decisions.parameter: AAPS max basal and max IOB limits
parameter_decisions.rationale: These ceilings are permissive relative to observed insulin use and deserve priority review, but they are not equivalent to delivered doses and lower derived caps were active in representative records. The package does not support exact replacement values.

Dynamic ISF materially strengthened some corrections and could contribute to later falls, but it also compensated for daytime rises. A sensitivity ratio of 1 is neutral, and Autosens remains explicitly disabled. No exact adjustment is supported without meal and complete dose histories.
No carbohydrates or COB series were recorded, so neither absorption setting can be tested. Delayed rises could also reflect meal timing, IOB, corrections, temporary targets or SMB/UAM.

meal_strategy_summary.suggestion: Do not infer a numerical prebolus or immediate bolus percentage from this dataset. For review, document those values for a recurring meal while keeping CR and automation stable, recognise that SMB/UAM may add insulin after a rise, and use regular announced carbs unless meal-linked evidence supports a separate e-carb amount, offset and duration.
meal_strategy_summary.rationale: No meal strategy, carbohydrate entry or e-carb entry was declared or observed. Daytime rises coexist with substantial automated IOB and delayed lows, so increasing immediate insulin or modelling delayed carbs without meal-linked evidence could misattribute the pattern.
meal_strategy_summary.next_observation: Record the same recurring meal on several comparable days with carbohydrate amount, meal and insulin timestamps, actual prebolus minutes, immediate bolus percentage, starting glucose and IOB, SMBs, corrections, activity, temporary targets, low treatments and CGM response through six hours.

exceptions.pattern: Daytime rise followed by a fall or low around 18:00-19:00
exceptions.suggestion: Review cumulative IOB and automated delivery before considering a stronger CR, larger immediate percentage or additional correction.
exceptions.rationale: Representative episodes show substantial IOB and glucose reductions exceeding 100 mg/dL over subsequent hours.

exceptions.pattern: A future documented meal shows a reproducible late rise after a limited early response
exceptions.suggestion: Compare regular announced carbs with a conservatively reviewed e-carb model while keeping other meal and automation settings unchanged.
exceptions.rationale: Only repeatable meal-linked evidence can separate delayed absorption from correction, temporary-target, SMB and IOB effects.

implementation_steps: Confirm that the authoritative profile and listed AAPS values still match the active device configuration before interpreting new observations.
Review severe and recurrent low episodes first, including independent glucose confirmation when feasible and the complete preceding insulin, temporary-target, meal and activity history.
Keep profile and automation values unchanged while collecting several fasting-like overnight observations from 21:00 to 08:00 with low starting IOB.
Review actual peak IOB, delivered basal rates and derived safety caps before considering any maximum IOB or maximum basal change; assess one limit at a time.
Only after overnight and automation review, record several comparable recurring meals through six hours without simultaneously changing CR, ISF, DIA, Dynamic ISF, SMB limits or absorption settings.
If a later change is independently supported, review and apply only one parameter at a time, then monitor its expected effect and hypoglycaemia exposure before considering another dependent setting.
education: Scheduled basal is not the same as delivered insulin in a closed-loop system because temporary basal, SMBs and suspensions can dominate total exposure.
A daytime high followed by a delayed low can reflect cumulative insulin rather than an insufficient basal rate or weak CR.
Dynamic ISF can make effective sensitivity stronger or weaker than the fixed profile ISF, so fixed ISF cannot be judged from correction outcomes alone.
Maximum IOB and maximum basal are safety ceilings, not routine doses; a high ceiling may still offer little backstop even when it is rarely reached.
UAM responds to glucose patterns without recorded COB and should not be interpreted as automatically counting COB twice.
E-carbs model carbohydrate absorption over time and are not a pump extended bolus.
safety_notes: This is decision-support content only and does not provide medical advice.
Every proposed review or change must be independently verified, discussed with the appropriate care team where applicable, made one at a time and followed with close glucose monitoring.
Recurrent or severe low readings warrant prompt attention under the user's established hypoglycaemia plan, with confirmatory measurement when appropriate and safe.
No AAPS or profile setting should be changed automatically from this analysis.
